description: Professional tennis singles, ATP and WTA main tour (Grand Slams, Tour Finals, 1000, 500, 250 events), seasons 2013-2021; one row per match; player A is assigned at random, so the task is symmetric: swapping A and B negates the odds column and every difference column, exchanges each _a/_b pair column and flips the label. Target: 1 if player A won. Inputs are pre-match only: odds_logit, the bookmakers' closing log-odds that A wins (de-vigged average of the books), which is by far the strongest input; differences (A minus B) of rating systems (overall Elo log-odds and the two players' surface offsets, serve/return strength ratings, games-weighted Elo), opponent-adjusted serve/return statistics over a two-week memory, long-memory offence/defence ratings per statistic on the match's surface, recent load and age; each player's matches on the surface earlier this season and days since his or her last match on it (_a/_b pairs); plus match context (tour, surface, indoor, level, best-of, round). The question is whether these inputs improve on the odds. Predictions will be for the later seasons 2022-2026 and are scored by log loss, so calibration matters.
